conflicts.issue: Proposed Ban on All Solicitation in Roadway Rights-of-Way
conflicts.summary: Committee members and legal counsel debated whether to adopt a local ordinance prohibiting all solicitation—including panhandling, charitable collections, and newspaper sales—in roadway rights-of-way, with Lewis A. Cheek and proponents emphasizing roadway safety and service referrals while another speaker raised First Amendment and livelihood concerns for newspaper vendors.
conflicts.side_a_position: Support a roadway right-of-way solicitation ban as a traffic safety measure paired with graduated citations and social service referrals.
side_a_arguments: Solicitation in roadway rights-of-way creates motor vehicle collision risks even where specific injury data is unavailable.
Existing permit and safety-vest requirements have not reduced roadway solicitation because solicitors are not purchasing permits.

Graduated enforcement (first-offense citation with service referrals and no fine or jail, escalating only upon repeat offenses) encourages individuals to seek help while charities have shifted to shopping centers off the roadway.
conflicts.side_b_position: Express caution over First Amendment limits, content-neutrality hurdles, and the impact on disabled or part-time newspaper vendors.
side_b_arguments: Legal counsel advised that the First Amendment prohibits a total ban on panhandling and prevents exempting Herald-Sun newspaper sellers or firefighter boot drives without creating indefensible content-based discrimination.
An opposing speaker questioned restricting First Amendment rights and noted that intersections fall within the City's geographical boundaries.
A blanket ban would displace regular morning newspaper vendors, including a disabled vendor at 15-501 and University Drive.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote was taken; the committee requested copies of the Raleigh and Chapel Hill solicitation ordinances for further review.

meetings.title: Joint City-County Committee Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 8, 2008 Joint City-County Committee meeting chaired by Ellen W. Reckhow, officials discussed joint youth initiatives, cable television access, community crime prevention, roadway solicitation restrictions, and Neighborhood College funding. Following unanimous voice-vote approval of the minutes (moved by Becky M. Heron and seconded by Lewis A. Cheek) and an update on the Animal Control Advisory Committee's work regarding animal chaining, staff reported securing a commitment from Time Warner Cable to restore Channel 8 public access programming and outlined an interlocal cost-sharing partnership for a joint City-County government PEG channel. Police Chief Chalmers presented a proposed Partners Against Crime (PAC) governance structure for Operation Bullseye, and committee members held an extended policy debate over a proposed ordinance banning solicitation in roadway rights-of-way—including First Amendment constraints against exempting newspaper vendors or charitable boot drives—without taking a vote, instead requesting Raleigh and Chapel Hill ordinances for review. Finally, after a fifth-year program update from Assistant County Manager Deborah Crocker and Ruby Hartgrave-Monds, the committee unanimously approved a $5 increase in the Neighborhood College student participation fee (moved by Eugene Brown and seconded by Bill Bell) to maintain its $5,000 budget.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks and Joint Youth Initiative Collaboration
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow opened the meeting and Council Member Eugene Brown commended her Sunday Herald-Sun article outlining a blueprint for youth. Reckhow noted the County Board's recent support for career center renovations and stressed the need for City-County collaboration with Mayor Bill Bell, while discussion also highlighted Operation Breakthrough's four-year planning and interest in expanding Head Start into Early Start.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes and Animal Control Advisory Committee Follow-Up
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The committee approved the prior meeting minutes unanimously by voice vote on a motion by Becky M. Heron and a second by Lewis A. Cheek. Chair Reckhow also asked for a five-to-six-month follow-up from the August meeting regarding dangerous dogs, and Heron reported that the Animal Control Advisory Committee is working on issues caused by the chaining of animals in the city and county.

agenda_items.title: Channel 8 Public Access and Joint City-County Government PEG Channel
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Patrick and County staff addressed two Time Warner Cable issues: restoring discontinued public access programming services on Channel 8, for which the City Manager secured a commitment from Time Warner representative Brad Phillips, and establishing a joint City-County government PEG channel via an interlocal agreement with shared budget costs. Reverend Vaughn of the Cable Advisory Committee thanked the City Manager for working with local pastors and producers, while staff noted City and County attorneys are jointly pressing Time Warner for a basic-tier channel assignment rather than a digital-tier slot.

agenda_items.title: Operation Bullseye Governance Structure under Partners Against Crime
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following brief remarks about pairing youth programming with parent engagement, Police Chief Chalmers presented a recommended governance structure placing Operation Bullseye under the Partners Against Crime (PAC) initiative. The proposal establishes an executive committee of five PAC facilitators plus one City and one County representative, an advisory committee based on the Northeast Central Durham Leadership Council (led by Earl Phillips) expanded across target neighborhoods, and task-force working groups supported by NECD and RBA staff.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Ordinance Prohibiting Solicitation in Roadway Rights-of-Way
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Committee members and legal counsel debated a proposed ordinance banning all solicitation—including panhandling, newspaper sales, and charitable collections—in roadway rights-of-way using graduated penalties starting with a service-referral citation and escalating to fines, suspended sentences, and potential jail time on a fourth offense. Legal counsel noted that under the First Amendment, a total ban on panhandling is impermissible and any roadway ban cannot exempt Herald-Sun vendors or firefighter boot drives without creating unconstitutional content-based discrimination, while an opposing speaker questioned limiting First Amendment rights and displacing disabled newspaper vendors. No vote was taken, and members asked to review the Raleigh and Chapel Hill statutes.

agenda_items.title: Neighborhood College Request to Increase Student Participation Fee
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant County Manager Deborah Crocker and Ruby Hartgrave-Monds presented a fifth-year update on the joint City-County Neighborhood College program, noting 22 enrolled participants toward a 25-person target and consistent adherence to past budgets. To offset slight cost increases and keep the spring semester within its $5,000 budget, staff requested a $5 increase in the student participation fee, which the committee approved unanimously before adjourning at 10:56 a.m.

votes.discussion_detail: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow called for approval of the previous meeting minutes. Motion was made by Becky M. Heron and seconded by Lewis A. Cheek, carrying unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Neighborhood College Request to Increase Student Participation Fee
votes.notes: No individual roll-call headcount was stated on the record during the voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Following a fifth-year budget presentation by Assistant County Manager Deborah Crocker and Ruby Hartgrave-Monds requesting a $5 participation fee increase to keep spring operations within $5,000, Eugene Brown moved approval and Bill Bell seconded, carrying unanimously by voice vote.
